chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Wasshash, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abdullah al-Lahham, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who buys the wife of a man from the People of Shirk to take her as his wife, and he said, 'There is no harm in it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a Muslim man to marry a woman from the People of Polytheism (Ahl al-Shirk)?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) permits a Muslim man to marry a woman from the *Ahl al-Shirk* (polytheists), specifically noting the context of acquiring her as a slave or concubine (*sariyyah*). This ruling highlights the flexibility in marital laws regarding non-Muslim women of the Book or polytheists in early Islamic jurisprudence, distinguishing it from the prohibition of marrying polytheist men to Muslim women. The chain of transmission through prominent figures like Ibn Bukayr and al-Wasshash underscores the reliability of this legal precedent in Shia fiqh.
